regexCodeList.string: (?:No Problem!|snickers nervously\.|looks a little worried about the idea\.|should be a fair fight!|chuckles at the thought of you fighting|would crush you like a bug!|would dance on your grave!|would be easy, but is it even worth the work out\?|BEGONE FROM MY SIGHT)

Script.name: consider
Script.script:
--[[ Consider Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01
'con all' rates everything in the room, one line of prose per mob. Past about three mobs that's a paragraph you have to read rather than glance at, and the thing you actually want - can I take it - is buried at the end of the sentence.
So the line gets rewritten where it stands: verdict first, colour-coded, then the level difference, the name, and any flags.
-5 (Golden Aura) No Problem! A guard of the Burh is weak compared to you. weak -5 A guard of the Burh (Golden Aura)
Aardwolf's verdicts, easiest to hardest. The MUD's own strings, all of them counted in 45 sessions of logs rather than remembered:
would be easy, but is it even worth the work out? You would stomp ... into the ground. No Problem! ... is weak compared to you. snickers nervously. looks a little worried about the idea. should be a fair fight! chuckles at the thought of you fighting would crush you like a bug! would dance on your grave! Best run away from ... while you can! You would be completely annihilated by ...! says 'BEGONE FROM MY SIGHT unworthy!'
The last three sit mid-sentence rather than after the mob, which is why NAME carries a different shape for them.
'con all' prefixes the level difference; plain 'consider <mob>' doesn't, so the number is optional. Flags are parenthesised before the verdict and there can be more than one.
Written from that output and Aardwolf's own messages. Not a port of Mushclient-Consider, which is GPL-3.0; see CREDITS.md. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.con = aardkit.con or {}
local C = aardkit.con local U = aardkit.util
local CFG = U.load("consider", { on = true })
-- label, colour, and the MUD wording that means it. Ranking is ours. -- Three of these were missing until a sweep of 45 sessions of logs turned them -- up: 'would stomp' (23 hits), 'Best run away from' (26) and 'completely -- annihilated by' (3). Without them those lines fell through unrecognised and -- printed raw, which looked like the module ignoring the hardest and easiest -- mobs in the room - exactly the ones you most want called out. local VERDICT = { { "trivial", "#5a7a5a", "would be easy, but is it even worth the work out%?" }, { "stomp", "#4f8f5f", "would stomp .* into the ground%." }, { "weak", "#3ad07a", "No Problem!" }, { "nervous", "#9ece6a", "snickers nervously%." }, { "worried", "#c8d05a", "looks a little worried about the idea%." }, { "fair", "#e0af68", "should be a fair fight!" }, { "hard", "#e08a68", "chuckles at the thought of you fighting" }, { "crushing", "#f7768e", "would crush you like a bug!" }, { "deadly", "#e94560", "would dance on your grave!" }, { "run", "#d1305a", "Best run away from .* while you can!" }, { "doomed", "#c02048", "would be completely annihilated by" }, { "no chance", "#b02a4a", "BEGONE FROM MY SIGHT" }, }
-- The three new ones put the mob in the middle of the sentence rather than at -- the front, so they don't fit the '^(.-) verb' shape the rest use. local NAME = { "^No Problem!%s*(.-) is weak compared to you%.$", "^You would stomp (.-) into the ground%.$", "^You would be completely annihilated by (.-)!$", "^Best run away from (.-) while you can!$", "^(.-) would be easy", "^(.-) snickers nervously", "^(.-) looks a little worried", "^(.-) should be a fair fight", "^(.-) chuckles at the thought", "^(.-) would crush you", "^(.-) would dance on your grave", "^(.-) says 'BEGONE", }
function C.on_line() if not CFG.on then return end
local line = U.trim(getCurrentLine() or "") if line == "" then return end
local label, colour for _, v in ipairs(VERDICT) do if line:find(v[3]) then label, colour = v[1], v[2]; break end end if not label then return end
-- optional level difference, then any number of (flag) groups local lvl, rest = line:match("^(%-?%d+)%s+(.*)$") rest = rest or line
local flags = {} while true do local f, tail = rest:match("^%((.-)%)%s*(.*)$") if not f then break end flags[#flags + 1] = f rest = tail end
local name for _, pat in ipairs(NAME) do name = rest:match(pat) if name and name ~= "" then break end end if not name or name == "" then return end
U.gag() -- leading newline: deleteLine leaves the cursor mid-line, so without it each -- mob concatenates onto the last one and the whole block reads as one line U.out(string.format("\n<%s>%-9s<r> <#8a93a8>%3s<r> <#c8d0dc>%s<r>%s", colour, label, lvl and (tonumber(lvl) > 0 and ("+" .. lvl) or lvl) or "", name, #flags > 0 and (" <#7aa2f7>(" .. table.concat(flags, ") (") .. ")<r>") or "")) end
function C.cmd(arg) local verb = U.split_verb(arg)
if verb == "" or verb == "status" then U.help("Consider", { { "rewriting", CFG.on and "on" or "off" }, { "" }, { "xcon on | off", "rewrite the lines, or leave the MUD's own" }, { "" }, { "Type 'con all' at the MUD; this tidies the answer in place." }, { "Verdict first and colour-coded, because 'can I take it' is the" }, { "point and the MUD buries it at the end of the sentence." }, })
elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then CFG.on = (verb == "on") U.save("consider", CFG) U.ok("Consider lines " .. (CFG.on and "rewritten." or "left as the MUD sends them."))
else U.warn("xcon [on|off]") end end
aardkit.register("xcon", "tidies what 'con all' says about the room", C.cmd)
